name: Magnetohydrodynamic Pulse Rifle MHPR-2 'Saltwater'
description:
The MHPR-2 generates a directed magnetohydrodynamic pulse — a propagating wave of coupled electromagnetic and fluid-dynamic force that interacts violently with any ionised or conductive medium in its path. In practical terms, this means the weapon is extraordinarily effective against targets in or near water, electrolyte-rich environments, or any surface where conductive fluid is present. Blood, sweat, hydraulic fluid, coolant lines, and saline-based biological tissue all become force-multiplying conductors when the pulse strikes.

The weapon's mechanism involves a two-stage barrel: the first stage aerosolises a fine mist of ionised saline solution ahead of the pulse (an internal reservoir holds approximately 40 shots worth of medium), and the second stage fires the MHD wave through the freshly conductive air column. The result is a propagating electromagnetic hammer that follows the conductive path with high fidelity. Against unprotected biological targets, the effect is described as a full-body cramp followed by vascular rupture in the extremities. Against electronics, it is effectively a targeted EMP with physical force components.

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS designed the MHPR-2 for naval interdiction and subsurface combat — environments where water is ambient and the weapon's medium requirement is naturally met. Field adaptation by operators working in humid, industrial, and sewage-adjacent environments has expanded its effective theatres considerably. The weapon has an unofficial reputation as the preferred tool of operators working the GLMZ canal district and the flooded sub-levels beneath the financial quarter.
specifications:
effective range: 8–35 metres (medium-dependent)
pulse frequency: Single shot, 2.4-second recharge cycle
saline reservoir: 40 shots (field-refillable with any electrolyte solution)
power source: MHD cell pack (60 pulses)
weight: 4.3 kg
form factor: Long-frame rifle with dual-barrel configuration and reservoir housing
environmental modifiers: Effectiveness increases 40–300% in high-humidity or wet conditions
electronics disruption: Hard EMP effect within 2 metres of pulse impact
tactical_use: Devastating in flooded environments, sewage tunnels, rain conditions, and near open water. Operators using Saltwater in dry conditions must rely on the onboard saline mist, which reduces effective range and gives targets a brief visible warning (the mist cloud). Experienced users pre-wet target surfaces or coordinate with team members who can introduce conductive medium before firing. The EMP side-effect makes it valuable for disabling drones, vehicle electronics, and cyberware — though the physical force component means targets near electronics will suffer simultaneously. Faraday suits reduce biological damage but do not protect electronics nearby.
cultural_context: Saltwater is almost exclusively associated with the canal districts and the drowned sub-levels — the flooded infrastructure beneath GLMZ's financial core that nobody officially acknowledges. The people who live and work in those spaces (unlicensed salvagers, pipe-gangs, sewer-runners, and the communities that have built permanent habitation in the flooded zones) treat the MHPR-2 with a mix of fear and respect. Military surplus units have trickled into those communities over decades, and a Saltwater in the hands of a canal operator signals serious territorial intent. Above ground, the weapon is rarely seen and widely misunderstood.
known_users: Canal district salvage crews operating contested territory
Corporate dive teams doing off-book infrastructure work
"Brine" — a semi-legendary canal district fixer who reportedly carries a modified MHPR-2 as her only weapon
story_hooks: A series of deaths in the flooded sub-levels show vascular rupture patterns consistent with MHPR-2 use — but the victims are members of three different pipe-gangs who have been at peace for two years. Someone is trying to restart the canal wars.

An ARCTURUS logistics manifest has surfaced showing a shipment of MHPR-2s destined for a classified naval program was diverted. Forty rifles are unaccounted for. The players are hired to find them before they flood (literally) into the civilian market.
A player character with significant cyberware is warned that someone in the canal district has a Saltwater and knows their route. They need to find a Faraday solution fast.

The flooded sub-levels community is requesting Saltwaters through a fixer network to defend against a corporate reclamation project. The players have to decide whether to supply them, who to source from, and what strings come attached.
